children: is taking its AI ambitions beyond Earth as SpaceX
prepares to launch satellites powered by the chipmaker's technology, creating a potential new source of demand for its accelerators.

SpaceX plans to begin launching the first AI satellites in the fourth quarter of 2027. Elon Musk has said orbital computing could eventually offer a different way to handle energy-intensive AI workloads, with the network targeted for broader deployment in 2028.

The relationship extends beyond hardware sales. Nvidia disclosed ownership of 122.8 million SpaceX shares, making the chipmaker both a supplier and shareholder. Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin systems are also being shipped to SpaceX alongside other major cloud customers.

The opportunity remains speculative. Analysts do not expect SpaceX's orbital computing operations to generate meaningful revenue until at least fiscal 2029, while technical issues involving heat removal, radiation exposure, satellite congestion and regulation could slow deployment.
SpaceX could become an additional long-term customer for Nvidia's AI systems, but the financial impact is likely to remain limited until orbital computing reaches commercial scale.

title: SpaceX Picks Nvidia Chips for Orbital AI. What It Means for NVDA Stock
